title: Make AI Agents Recommend Your Product - AgentRel Playbook
content:
Your next customer might not Google you.
They might ask ChatGPT or Claude which
clinic, shop, or SaaS to use.
If your product is invisible to agents,
you lose the shortlist before the human
ever sees you.
Today I will show a practical AGENTREL
PLAYBOOK you can start this week.

It ties to Manicule, the YC P26 company
building AgentRel for developer tools.
I do not work with them. I am translating
the thesis for clinics, shops, and SaaS
owners.
Stay for the free checklist CTA at the end.

Here is the shift in plain English.
Search used to be 10 blue links.
Now a prompt returns 2 or 3
recommendations with a reason.
Agents pick from public docs, FAQs,
comparisons, and tool descriptions they
can parse.
If your site is marketing fluff with no
structure, the model skips you or invents
features you never shipped.

Step 1. Write DOCS AGENTS CAN PARSE.
Clear H2 headings. 1 page per outcome.
Working examples.
Say what the product does, who it is for,
and what it does not do.
Imagine a clinic: publish service pages
with hours, booking steps, and insurance
rules in plain text, not only in images.
Say a SaaS shop: publish an API overview
and a "when to use us vs when not" page.

Step 2. Structure FAQs around real prompts.
People ask AI: cheapest option, fastest
setup, works with WhatsApp, needs a human,
refund policy.
Your FAQ should answer those exact
questions in short paragraphs.
If the answer depends on a human decision, say so.
That honesty helps agents recommend you
for the right jobs.

Step 3. Clear tool descriptions, plus
HUMAN APPROVAL for irreversible actions.
If you expose tools to agents, name inputs
and outputs tightly.
Do not let an agent invent a discount, a
delivery date, or a medical claim.
Score and draft is fine. Send, book,
charge, or diagnose stays behind a human
tap.
That is how AgentRel becomes trust, not spam.

Imagine you run a boutique agency or a local shop.
This weekend you ask ChatGPT for the best
option in your category without naming
yourself.
Then you ask again with your brand name.
You fix every wrong fact in public docs
within 48 hours.
That single loop is more useful than
another ad creative.

Here's my take.
AgentRel is not a new marketing department
name. It is technical clarity plus
distribution for a new buyer: the agent.
Start with docs, FAQs, and tool descriptions.
Keep a human on irreversible sends.
If you want this playbook for your clinic,
shop, or SaaS, DM ME.

Comment 'AI' on Instagram and I'll send
you the free checklist, or grab the link
in the LinkedIn post.
Follow for your daily AI update.
